title: Program Kit capability consumer integration postures
intent: Let each consumer product explicitly choose no provider integration, contributor-local optional integration, or repository-managed integration while Program Kit supplies only reviewed adapters, deterministic project-scoped mechanics, exact multi-provider ownership, safe migration and removal, and clear documentation.
scope: Three documented consumer-owned integration postures: none, local-optional, and repository-managed.
Reviewed Codex and Claude Code project-skill discovery roots and thin adapter output.
A versioned multi-provider capability ownership lock with exact legacy migration.
Explicit exact-byte provider removal and transactional project-contained mutation.
Capability bundle, canonical capability, provider-adapter, CLI, test, and consumer-onboarding updates.
Migration of the Domain Semantic Engine consumer to the current Codex repository-skill location while preserving its repository-managed Codex posture.
nonGoals: Selecting or enforcing a consumer posture from Program Kit.
Changing consumer .gitignore files, staging or committing consumer files, installing a provider globally, granting provider trust or permissions, or starting development work.
Adding an unreviewed provider, guessing an adapter from a folder convention, or turning provider adapters into canonical capability sources.
Loading capability prose or provider configuration from runtime libraries or generated applications.
Creating hooks, watchers, startup tasks, MCP bindings, tool bindings, autonomous loops, release behavior, deployment behavior, or package-feed publication.
Modifying or adopting the unrelated web-publication-static-react worktree.
assumptions: Official Codex repository-skill discovery remains .agents/skills through implementation; material provider-contract drift stops the affected work unit.
Official Claude Code project-skill discovery remains .claude/skills through implementation; material provider-contract drift stops the affected work unit.
The current pending Domain Semantic Engine CapabilityBundle 3.0.0 consumer initialization is preserved as human work and superseded coherently only after the new bundle is verified.
The existing private Program Kit C# gate remains compatible with Program Kit-owned implementation.

domains.purpose: Own deterministic consumer-workspace projection of reviewed Program Kit capability adapters without owning consumer repository policy, provider authority, or runtime behavior.

vocabulary.meaning: A consumer-owned documented choice among none, local-optional, and repository-managed capability-provider integration.
The exact set of thin Program Kit-owned wrappers rendered for one reviewed provider beneath one consumer workspace.
One versioned project-contained record that binds every Program Kit-owned provider wrapper to exact canonical, template, output, bundle, and manifest bytes.
A provider adapter whose complete discovery contract, template, output root, compatibility boundary, tests, documentation, and CLI registration have been explicitly reviewed.

semanticModels.meaning: The consumer README declaration that distinguishes intentional absence, contributor-local optional setup, and committed repository-managed provider discovery.
semanticModels.invariants: Program Kit documents the finite options but never selects, persists, enforces, or infers the posture.

semanticModels.meaning: The exact finite set of reviewed provider bindings currently owned by Program Kit in one consumer workspace.
semanticModels.invariants: Every owned output appears exactly once, all provider identifiers and paths are reviewed and normalized, and no exact binding disappears except through explicit exact-byte removal.

artifactDecisions.requestedOutcome: Represent the approved posture options, reviewed-provider boundary, multi-provider ownership, migration, exact removal, compatibility, and verification obligations as one canonical review design.

executableBehavior.rationale: The design grants no initialization, removal, provider, Git, runtime, package, or implementation authority.

valueLifecycle.rationale: Canonical bytes are schema-validated, semantically checked, digest-bound by Planning 3.0 and the review manifest, and rechecked before implementation.

agentRetrieval.rationale: The review set is explicit repository input; it does not create or register a provider capability.

agentProcedure.rationale: Prospective initializer and remover mechanics are product work units, not active agent procedures.

humanCommunication.audience: The human Program Kit reviewer, consumer product owners, contributors, and the bounded implementer.
humanCommunication.decisionAuthorityBoundary: Only explicit human approval of this review-set version and exact canonical design and plan SHA-256 values authorizes implementation.
humanCommunication.rationale: Canonical JSON, reviewer projections, provider evidence, source baseline, static disposition, implementation plan, and validation report expose the complete decision.

governance.provenancePolicy: Exact human intent, provider-contract evidence, current Program Kit source bytes, pending consumer initialization, and excluded concurrent work are named.
governance.digestPolicy: The review manifest and Planning 3.0 plan bind exact canonical bytes; any material change requires revalidation, new digests, and renewed human approval.
governance.compatibilityPolicy: Provider identifiers and discovery roots, lock versions, capability-bundle revisions, canonical capability bytes, adapter templates, CLI grammar, diagnostics, migrations, and consumer documentation version explicitly.
governance.migrationPolicy: Legacy single-provider locks and legacy Codex paths migrate only from exact owned bytes during explicit initialization or removal; incompatible or ambiguous state stops without partial mutation.

dataHandling.redactionPolicy: Artifacts contain repository-relative paths, identities, versions, digests, provider identifiers, and public documentation URLs only; credentials, prompts, transcripts, environment values, and secret values are excluded.
dataHandling.externalizationPolicy: Canonical capability semantics remain Program Kit-owned; thin wrappers and ownership evidence may be committed only by explicit consumer policy.
dataHandling.ephemeralDataPolicy: Provider sessions, trust prompts, local ignore configuration, Git index state, and runtime state are observations outside the durable design.

artifactDecisions.rationale: One canonical design keeps Program Kit mechanics, consumer repository policy, provider discovery, human authority, migration, and runtime isolation distinct.

security.policy: Verify exact bundle, canonical, template, lock, and existing output bytes before project-contained mutation.
guarantees: Unsupported providers, path escape, user-global roots, collision, tamper, incomplete bundles, and invalid locks fail closed.
Wrappers remain thin and contain one portable canonical pointer.
exclusions: No credential, provider trust, permission, secret, user-global configuration, or arbitrary script installation.

authority.policy: The consumer owns posture and Git policy; a human explicitly starts each initialization, removal, and development request.
guarantees: Program Kit exposes finite mechanics and documentation without selecting a posture.
Initialization and committed wrappers grant no development authority.
exclusions: No silent initialization, provider selection, work initiation, staging, commit, trust, permission, or global installation.

secrets.policy: Capability integration stores no secret values or provider credentials.
guarantees: Locks and diagnostics contain only normalized paths, provider IDs, versions, and digests.
exclusions: No secret discovery, persistence, redaction inference, transcript capture, or environment capture.

persistence.policy: Persist only exact provider wrapper bytes and one project-contained ownership lock selected by explicit human operations.
guarantees: Every owned provider remains represented until exact explicit removal.
Transactions preserve unrelated provider files and recover or fail without ambiguous partial ownership.
exclusions: No .gitignore, Git index, Git commit, provider-global root, runtime package, or application-state mutation.

failure.policy: Fail closed before externally visible partial mutation when source, ownership, provider, path, compatibility, or recovery state is invalid.
guarantees: Stable diagnostics distinguish unsupported provider, invalid source, collision, tamper, migration refusal, and transaction recovery.
Human-owned or modified files remain unchanged.
exclusions: No guessed ownership, silent overwrite, silent removal, fallback provider path, or inferred success.

concurrency.policy: One workspace capability transaction owns the lock mutation boundary at a time.
guarantees: Concurrent or abandoned transaction state is detected before mutation.
exclusions: No last-writer-wins lock replacement, unbounded retry, or concurrent provider mutation.

cancellation.policy: Cancellation is honored before commit; after commit begins, recovery evidence determines the exact final state.
guarantees: Cancellation never leaves owned wrappers without corresponding ownership evidence.
exclusions: No claim that arbitrary filesystem failures are reversible without a valid transaction record.

observability.policy: Expose deterministic success or stable diagnostics and exact ownership-lock bytes without recording prompts or provider sessions.
guarantees: Tests can observe provider set, output paths, migrations, removals, bundle binding, and unrelated-byte preservation.
exclusions: No prompt, reasoning trace, credential, transcript, environment, or provider-session recording.

compatibility.policy: Version lock shape, bundle revision, provider roots, CLI grammar, diagnostics, and canonical capability mappings explicitly.
guarantees: Legacy version 1 locks remain readable only for exact explicit migration.
The Codex .codex/skills to .agents/skills move is ownership-verified and non-destructive.
exclusions: No floating provider contract, silent bundle upgrade, ambiguous legacy acceptance, or indefinite dual-path claim.

scenarios.intent: Choose and clearly communicate how Program Kit AI development capabilities are exposed.
preconditions: The product uses Program Kit or chooses whether to expose its development capabilities.
steps: State the choice in the consumer README.
Link to the exact pinned Program Kit capability setup documentation.
For repository-managed, explicitly initialize and review each selected provider binding before committing it.
outcomes: A contributor can distinguish intentional absence from incomplete setup.
Program Kit has not selected policy or modified Git state.
failureOutcomes: A bare Program Kit link without a consumer-specific posture statement is incomplete onboarding.
An unsupported provider or unreviewed adapter remains unavailable.

scenarios.intent: Initialize one reviewed provider without losing ownership of existing providers.
preconditions: The workspace and exact capability-bundle root are explicit.
Existing lock and wrapper bytes are valid or absent.
steps: Verify source, existing ownership, collisions, containment, and transaction state.
Render thin wrappers to the provider's current project root.
Commit wrapper and multi-provider lock bytes as one transaction.
outcomes: The selected provider is added or updated idempotently.
Other exact owned provider bindings remain represented and unchanged unless exact migration is required.
failureOutcomes: Tamper, collision, unsupported provider, provider-contract drift, path escape, invalid source, or ambiguous recovery stops without unowned mutation.

scenarios.intent: Explicitly remove one Program Kit-owned provider binding.
preconditions: The selected provider exists in a valid ownership lock.
Every selected wrapper still matches the exact lock-owned digest.
steps: Verify every owned output and transaction boundary.
Delete only exact owned wrapper files.
Update the provider set or remove the lock when the set becomes empty.
outcomes: No unrelated provider or human-owned file changes.
The workspace may intentionally return to the none posture.
failureOutcomes: Modified, missing, unowned, or ambiguous output stops removal without partial mutation.

scenarios.intent: Move an exact legacy Codex binding to the current repository-skill location.
preconditions: A valid version 1 single-provider lock owns exact .codex/skills wrapper bytes.
steps: Run explicit Codex initialization against the selected exact bundle.
Verify all legacy source and output bytes.
Remove only exact legacy owned wrapper files and write the version 2 multi-provider lock transactionally.
outcomes: Codex discovery follows the current reviewed repository contract.
No human-modified legacy file is overwritten or removed.
failureOutcomes: Invalid lock, changed legacy wrapper, target collision, or provider-contract drift stops migration.

statusClaims.claim: A candidate review design exists from explicit human intent, current provider evidence, and current Program Kit source truth; no initializer, remover, adapter, lock, bundle, consumer migration, provider action, or runtime behavior is implemented by this artifact.
